statement: The function returns a result r equal to the maximum number of fish catchable from one connected water region. A water cell is a cell (i,j) with grid[i][j] > 0. Two water cells are edge-adjacent if they differ by 1 in exactly one coordinate and are equal in the other; the water component of a water cell p is the set of all water cells reachable from p by a finite sequence of edge-adjacent moves. If grid has no water cell, then r = 0. Otherwise, r is the largest value of sum_{(i,j) in C} grid[i][j] over all water components C of grid; equivalently, there exists a water cell p whose water component has sum r, and every water cell q has water-component sum at most r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: For every grid satisfying the preconditions, find_max_fish returns a result; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r with 0 <= r <= sum_{i=0}^{m-1} sum_{j=0}^{n-1} grid[i][j].
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r, and for every cell (i,j) with 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n, grid[i][j] <= r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if grid[i][j] = 0 for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r equal to the sum of grid[i][j] over all water cells (i,j) of the grid.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Also, there is at least one water cell (a cell with positive value), and all water cells lie in a single water component, where two water cells are edge-adjacent if they differ by 1 in exactly one coordinate and are equal in the other.

statement: The function returns a result r. Call an interval [l,u] of column indices a maximal positive interval if 0 <= l <= u < n, grid[0][k] > 0 for every k with l <= k <= u, either l = 0 or grid[0][l-1] = 0, and either u = n-1 or grid[0][u+1] = 0. Then r is the maximum of the sums sum_{k=l}^{u} grid[0][k] over all maximal positive intervals [l,u], with the convention that this maximum is 0 if there is no maximal positive interval.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Additionally m = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r. Call an interval [l,u] of row indices a maximal positive interval if 0 <= l <= u < m, grid[k][0] > 0 for every k with l <= k <= u, either l = 0 or grid[l-1][0] = 0, and either u = m-1 or grid[u+1][0] = 0. Then r is the maximum of the sums sum_{k=l}^{u} grid[k][0] over all maximal positive intervals [l,u], with the convention that this maximum is 0 if there is no maximal positive interval.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Additionally n = 1.

statement: The function returns a result r for grid. Define gridT by gridT[j][i] = grid[i][j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Then find_max_fish(gridT) returns a result rT with rT = r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r for grid. Define gridR by gridR[i][j] = grid[m-1-i][n-1-j] for 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Then find_max_fish(gridR) returns a result rR with rR = r.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The call find_max_fish(grid) returns a result r, the call find_max_fish(h) returns a result r', and r <= r'.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). Both grid and h are non-empty rectangular m x n matrices with 1 <= m <= 10 and 1 <= n <= 10, all entries lie in the range 0 to 10, and grid[i][j] <= h[i][j] for every 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.

statement: The function returns a result r, and there exists a water cell (r0,c0) with 0 <= r0 < m, 0 <= c0 < n, and grid[r0][c0] > 0 such that r equals the sum of grid[i][j] over all water cells (i,j) reachable from (r0,c0) by a finite sequence of edge-adjacent water cells, including (r0,c0) itself. Two water cells are edge-adjacent if they differ by 1 in exactly one coordinate and are equal in the other.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n. Also, there is at least one water cell (a cell with positive value).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every cell (r0,c0) with 0 <= r0 < m, 0 <= c0 < n, and grid[r0][c0] > 0, the sum of grid[i][j] over all water cells (i,j) reachable from (r0,c0) by a finite sequence of edge-adjacent water cells, including (r0,c0) itself, is at most r. Two water cells are edge-adjacent if they differ by 1 in exactly one coordinate and are equal in the other.
preconditions: Let m = len(grid). The grid is non-empty and rectangular: 1 <= m <= 10, every row has the same length n with 1 <= n <= 10, so len(grid[i]) = n for all 0 <= i < m, and 0 <= grid[i][j] <= 10 for all 0 <= i < m and 0 <= j < n.
